excerpt: cult.fit (formerly CureFit) runs gyms, group classes and at-home workouts across India. cultpass PRO starts at about Rs 754/month on a 24-month plan.
content:
cult.fit, the company formerly called CureFit Healthcare, runs fitness centres, group workout classes and at-home live workouts under the cultpass membership, and sells fitness products through its cultsport brand. Its website lists cultpass ELITE (unlimited access to all its gyms in a city plus group classes), cultpass PRO (unlimited access to PRO gyms with credits for ELITE gyms and classes) and cultpass HOME, plus programmes such as cult Transform.

Entrepreneur India reported that Mukesh Bansal founded the company in 2016 with Ankit Nagori, both formerly of Flipkart (Bansal had cofounded Myntra), and that Naresh Krishnaswamy, also a cofounder, now leads it as CEO while Bansal moved to executive chairman. TechCrunch reported in June 2021 that Tata Digital agreed to invest up to USD 75 million in CureFit, and Entrepreneur India reported that a USD 100 million deal in November 2021, in which Zomato took a 6.4% stake, made the company a unicorn.

In July 2026 the company, now Cult.fit Limited, filed draft IPO papers with SEBI. Business Today reported a fresh issue of up to Rs 950 crore plus an offer for sale of up to 17,86,09,200 shares, and, citing Redseer, 708 fitness centres across 77 cities as of 31 March 2026, 987,020 transacting paid members in FY26 and revenue from operations of Rs 1,720.61 crore in FY26. Fitness services made up about 70% of revenue and products about 30%.

cultpass PRO prices are published on cult.fit and fall the longer you commit; the page itself shows two slightly different sets of figures, so confirm the price at checkout. This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product for this page, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.platform: Gyms and centres in India, plus Android and iOS apps
profile.starts_at: cultpass PRO from about Rs 754/month (24-month plan)
profile.summary_short: Gyms, group classes and at-home workouts across India under the cultpass membership

gallery.alt: Three women doing a yoga stretch on mats in a dimly lit cult.fit studio
A woman holding a loaded barbell with cult-branded plates in a gym

use_cases: Gym access in your city with cultpass ELITE or PRO
Group workout classes at cult centres
Live and recorded workouts at home
Training in another city while travelling, using the plan's other-city sessions

fit: live in one of the cities where cult.fit runs centres and want gyms plus group classes
are ready to commit for 6 to 24 months, where the monthly price is lowest
not_fit: only want a short trial: the 1-month option on the page lists workout videos, not gym access
live somewhere without a cult centre

pricing.intro: cultpass PRO prices from cult.fit, checked on 15 October 2026. The page shows two sets of figures (plan cards and a 'Choose your Cultpass' grid) that differ slightly; prices may vary by city, so confirm at checkout. ELITE prices are not shown on the same page.

plans.name: cultpass PRO, 24 months
plans.detail: 120 pause days, 120 other-city sessions, 200 ELITE credits

plans.name: cultpass PRO, 12 months
plans.detail: 60 pause days, 60 other-city sessions, 100 ELITE credits, two 1:1 trainer sessions

plans.name: cultpass PRO, 6 months
plans.detail: 30 pause days, 30 other-city sessions, 50 ELITE credits

plans.name: cultpass PRO, 3 months
plans.detail: 10 pause days, 15 other-city sessions, 30 ELITE credits

plans.name: cultpass ELITE
plans.price: Shown on cult.fit for your city
plans.detail: Unlimited access to all gyms in your city and unlimited group classes

pros: Large network: 708 centres in 77 cities (Redseer, via Business Today, March 2026)
Long plans bring the monthly cost down sharply
Pause days and other-city sessions included
cons: The pricing page shows two different sets of PRO prices
Best value needs a long commitment

alternatives.intro: Other fitness options in India. Prices are on each provider's own site.

items.name: Anytime Fitness
items.difference: Single-gym memberships with 24-hour access rather than a city-wide pass.

items.name: HealthifyMe
items.difference: App-based coaching with no gyms of its own.

items.name: Fitpass
items.difference: Pass that works across partner gyms.

faq.a: Mukesh Bansal and Ankit Nagori founded it in 2016, according to Entrepreneur India, which also names Naresh Krishnaswamy as a cofounder and current CEO.
cult.fit lists PRO from about Rs 754 a month on a 24-month plan; the 12-month plan is Rs 12,190 on the plan cards. Confirm at checkout.
It filed a draft red herring prospectus with SEBI in July 2026 for an IPO with a fresh issue of up to Rs 950 crore.

faq.q: How many centres does cult.fit have?
faq.a: 708 fitness centres across 77 cities as of 31 March 2026, per Redseer data cited in its IPO filing coverage.
